title: EigenOrbit Releases Open-Source eigenkit 1.0 for Multi-Backend Quantum Execution - Quantum Computing Report
gist: EigenOrbit released eigenkit 1.0, an Apache 2.0 Python library that lets developers write quantum algorithms once and run them on eight simulators and four QPU access points, with PyTorch and scikit-learn integration and built-in classical-versus-quantum benchmarking.

insights.claim: EigenOrbit's eigenkit 1.0 is an Apache 2.0-licensed Python library, installable via pip, for writing quantum algorithms once and executing them across multiple simulators and hardware backends without code modification.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Open-source portability layers erode lock-in to any single quantum SDK or cloud.

insights.claim: The framework abstracts hardware compilation behind a single provider argument, so switching backend requires changing one parameter.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Lower switching cost makes QPU vendors compete on performance and price rather than on software ecosystem.

insights.claim: eigenkit supports eight classical simulators (NumPy, PennyLane, Qiskit, Qiskit Aer, Qulacs, qsim, TensorCircuit, NVIDIA CUDA-Q) and four QPU access points: IBM Qiskit Runtime, IQM Resonance, Amazon Braket, and Quandela Perceval.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Backend coverage shows which vendors are reachable as standard targets, notably including a photonic platform (Quandela).

insights.claim: eigenkit connects PyTorch nn.Module layers and scikit-learn estimators to quantum backends, targeting machine-learning pipelines.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum machine learning tooling is converging on standard ML interfaces, lowering adoption friction for ML teams.

insights.claim: The library includes built-in classical-versus-quantum benchmarking with Wilcoxon statistical significance testing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Statistical benchmarking against classical baselines is a practical check on quantum advantage claims.

insights.claim: eigenkit issues automated pre-submission cost warnings for billable QPU hardware jobs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals that QPU access is metered and cost control is a real developer concern.
